title: Automate Certificates and HTTPS
objective: Automate self-signed and publicly trusted certificates with idempotent web-server configuration.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original companion material covering self-signed certificates, Let's Encrypt roles, DNS, inventory, and Nginx proxying.

paragraphs: TLS needs a private key, certificate, correct permissions, and web-server configuration. Self-signed certificates are useful in controlled labs but produce trust warnings unless their issuer is distributed as trusted.

ACME services such as Let's Encrypt validate domain control and issue publicly trusted certificates. Automation must account for DNS, reachable challenge paths, renewal, and safe secret handling. A reviewed Galaxy role can reduce duplication.
Nginx can terminate HTTPS and proxy traffic to an application. Templates should notify a reload handler and validate configuration before activation so a bad edit does not interrupt service.
explanation.rule: Automate renewal and validate web-server configuration before every reload.

examples.title: TLS File Intent
examples.code:
tls:
  certificate: /etc/ssl/certs/app.crt
  private_key: /etc/ssl/private/app.key
  key_mode: '0600'
  renew: true
examples.note: Private keys require tighter permissions than public certificates.

checks.question: What must an ACME client prove?

feedback.incorrect: Public CAs validate control over the domain name.

assignment.title: Describe TLS Assets
assignment.brief: Set certificate and private-key paths, mode 0600, and automated renewal.
requirements: Use separate certificate and key paths, restrictive mode, and renew true.
